title: Verb Types (る, う or Irregular?)
description: Learn to tell a verb's type from its dictionary form — the first step for every conjugation.

points.title: Doesn't end in る → う-verb
points.summary: 書く, 話す, 待つ, 死ぬ, 遊ぶ, 読む, 泳ぐ, 買う: always う-verbs.
points.body:
**How to tell the verb type** — look at the dictionary form:

- Doesn't end in る (〜う, 〜く, 〜す, 〜つ …) → **う-verb**, always.
- Ends in る, and the sound before it is **a / u / o** (分**か**る, 作**る**→つく**る**, 乗**る**) → **う-verb**, always.
- Ends in **-iる / -eる** (見る, 起**き**る, 食**べ**る) → usually a **る-verb**.
- …except a short list of common う-verbs: **帰る, 入る, 走る, 切る, 知る, 要る, 限る, 喋る, 滑る, 焦る, 減る, 蹴る, 握る, 散る**.
- **する** and **来る** are irregular; 勉強する and other noun + する verbs conjugate like する.

**Why it matters**
- る-verbs drop る: 食べ**ない**, 食べ**ます**, 食べ**て**.
- う-verbs change the last sound: 帰**ら**ない, 帰**り**ます, 帰**って**.

**Check yourself:** if you know the ない-form, it tells you the type — 帰**ら**ない has an あ-row sound, so 帰る is an う-verb.

points.title: -iる / -eる → usually る-verb
points.summary: 見る, 起きる, 食べる, 教える: drop る for every form.

points.summary: 分かる, 作る, 乗る, 取る: the sound before る is not i or e, so it's an う-verb.

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{書|か}く**?
questions.explanation:
{書|か}く ends in く, not る. Every verb that doesn't end in る is an う-verb: 書かない, 書きます, 書いて.

Example: {毎日|まいにち}{日記|にっき}を**{書|か}いて**います。
notes: Only verbs ending in る can be る-verbs.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: I keep a diary every day. (書く = to write)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{食|た}べる**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is べ (-e), and -iる / -eる verbs are normally る-verbs: just drop る → 食べない, 食べます, 食べて.

Example: {朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}を**{食|た}べない**{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えた。
notes: An う-verb would turn る into ら: 食べらない — but it's 食べない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: More people skip breakfast. (食べる = to eat)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{分|わ}かる**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is か (-a). Verbs in -aる are always う-verbs: 分からない, 分かります, 分かって.

Example: すみません、よく**{分|わ}かりません**。
notes: A る-verb would just drop る: 分かない — but it's 分からない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: Sorry, I don't really understand. (分かる = to understand)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **する**?
questions.explanation:
する is one of only two irregular verbs: しない, します, して.

Example: {週末|しゅうまつ}はテニスを**します**。
notes: It doesn't follow the regular pattern: しない, します, して.
It doesn't follow the regular pattern: しない, します, して.
questions.translation: I play tennis at weekends. (する = to do)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{話|はな}す**?
questions.explanation:
{話|はな}す ends in す, not る. Every verb that doesn't end in る is an う-verb: 話さない, 話します, 話して.

Example: {電話|でんわ}で{母|はは}と**{話|はな}した**。
notes: Only verbs ending in る can be る-verbs.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: I talked to my mother on the phone. (話す = to speak)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{見|み}る**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is み (-i), and -iる / -eる verbs are normally る-verbs: just drop る → 見ない, 見ます, 見て.

Example: {昨日|きのう}、{映画|えいが}を**{見|み}た**。
notes: An う-verb would turn る into ら: 見らない — but it's 見ない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: I saw a film yesterday. (見る = to see)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{作|つく}る**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is く (-u). Verbs in -uる are always う-verbs: 作らない, 作ります, 作って.

Example: {日曜日|にちようび}にケーキを**{作|つく}った**。
notes: A る-verb would just drop る: 作ない — but it's 作らない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: I made a cake on Sunday. (作る = to make)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{来|く}る**?
questions.explanation:
来る is irregular — its vowel changes: 来ない, 来ます, 来て (こない, きます, きて).

Example: {田中|たなか}さんはまだ**{来|こ}ない**。
notes: It doesn't follow the regular pattern: 来ない, 来ます, 来て.
It doesn't follow the regular pattern: 来ない, 来ます, 来て.
questions.translation: Tanaka still hasn't come. (来る = to come)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{待|ま}つ**?
questions.explanation:
{待|ま}つ ends in つ, not る. Every verb that doesn't end in る is an う-verb: 待たない, 待ちます, 待って.

Example: {駅|えき}の{前|まえ}で**{待|ま}って**います。
notes: Only verbs ending in る can be る-verbs.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: I'm waiting in front of the station. (待つ = to wait)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{起|お}きる**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is き (-i), and -iる / -eる verbs are normally る-verbs: just drop る → 起きない, 起きます, 起きて.

Example: {毎朝|まいあさ}6{時|じ}に**{起|お}きます**。
notes: An う-verb would turn る into ら: 起きらない — but it's 起きない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: I get up at six every morning. (起きる = to get up)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{乗|の}る**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is の (-o). Verbs in -oる are always う-verbs: 乗らない, 乗ります, 乗って.

Example: {毎朝|まいあさ}バスに**{乗|の}って**{会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}く。
notes: A る-verb would just drop る: 乗ない — but it's 乗らない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: I take the bus to work every morning. (乗る = to ride)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{勉強|べんきょう}する**?
questions.explanation:
{勉強|べんきょう}する is noun + する, so it conjugates exactly like する: 勉強しない, 勉強します, 勉強して.

Example: {毎晩|まいばん}{日本語|にほんご}を**{勉強|べんきょう}して**います。
notes: It doesn't follow the regular pattern: 勉強しない, 勉強します, 勉強して.
It doesn't follow the regular pattern: 勉強しない, 勉強します, 勉強して.
questions.translation: I study Japanese every evening. (勉強する = to study)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{死|し}ぬ**?
questions.explanation:
{死|し}ぬ ends in ぬ, not る. Every verb that doesn't end in る is an う-verb: 死なない, 死にます, 死んで.

Example: {飼|か}っていた{金魚|きんぎょ}が**{死|し}んで**しまった。
notes: Only verbs ending in る can be る-verbs.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: My goldfish died. (死ぬ = to die)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{教|おし}える**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is え (-e), and -iる / -eる verbs are normally る-verbs: just drop る → 教えない, 教えます, 教えて.

Example: {駅|えき}までの{道|みち}を**{教|おし}えて**ください。
notes: An う-verb would turn る into ら: 教えらない — but it's 教えない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: Please tell me the way to the station. (教える = to teach)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{取|と}る**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is と (-o). Verbs in -oる are always う-verbs: 取らない, 取ります, 取って.

Example: {塩|しお}を**{取|と}って**ください。
notes: A る-verb would just drop る: 取ない — but it's 取らない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: Please pass the salt. (取る = to take)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{遊|あそ}ぶ**?
questions.explanation:
{遊|あそ}ぶ ends in ぶ, not る. Every verb that doesn't end in る is an う-verb: 遊ばない, 遊びます, 遊んで.

Example: {子供|こども}たちが{公園|こうえん}で**{遊|あそ}んで**いる。
notes: Only verbs ending in る can be る-verbs.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: The children are playing in the park. (遊ぶ = to play)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{借|か}りる**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is り (-i), and -iる / -eる verbs are normally る-verbs: just drop る → 借りない, 借ります, 借りて.

Example: {友達|ともだち}に{傘|かさ}を**{借|か}りた**。
notes: An う-verb would turn る into ら: 借りらない — but it's 借りない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: I borrowed an umbrella from a friend. (借りる = to borrow)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{座|すわ}る**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is わ (-a). Verbs in -aる are always う-verbs: 座らない, 座ります, 座って.

Example: どうぞ、ここに**{座|すわ}って**ください。
notes: A る-verb would just drop る: 座ない — but it's 座らない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: Please, have a seat here. (座る = to sit)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{泳|およ}ぐ**?
questions.explanation:
{泳|およ}ぐ ends in ぐ, not る. Every verb that doesn't end in る is an う-verb: 泳がない, 泳ぎます, 泳いで.

Example: {夏|なつ}は{毎日|まいにち}{海|うみ}で**{泳|およ}いだ**。
notes: Only verbs ending in る can be る-verbs.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: I swam in the sea every day in summer. (泳ぐ = to swim)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{忘|わす}れる**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is れ (-e), and -iる / -eる verbs are normally る-verbs: just drop る → 忘れない, 忘れます, 忘れて.

Example: {傘|かさ}を{電車|でんしゃ}に**{忘|わす}れた**。
notes: An う-verb would turn る into ら: 忘れらない — but it's 忘れない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: I left my umbrella on the train. (忘れる = to forget)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{買|か}う**?
questions.explanation:
{買|か}う ends in う, not る. Every verb that doesn't end in る is an う-verb: 買わない, 買います, 買って.

Example: {駅前|えきまえ}の{店|みせ}でパンを**{買|か}った**。
notes: Only verbs ending in る can be る-verbs.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: I bought bread at the shop by the station. (買う = to buy)

questions.prompt: What type of verb is **{閉|し}める**?
questions.explanation:
The sound before る is め (-e), and -iる / -eる verbs are normally る-verbs: just drop る → 閉めない, 閉めます, 閉めて.

Example: {寒|さむ}いので、{窓|まど}を**{閉|し}めて**ください。
notes: An う-verb would turn る into ら: 閉めらない — but it's 閉めない.
Only する (with noun + する verbs) and 来る are irregular.
questions.translation: It's cold, so please close the window. (閉める = to close)
